relations.quote: The layer expresses its phase frames through the [complex phase network](complex-phase-network.md), as products of $C$ on the selected bits.
The layer moves its address chunks by [address-field interchange](address-interchange.md), a tape procedure.
The layer applies the length-two case of the [discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) to each selected bit.
The layer is the tensor power of $H_0$ on the selected bits, written $H_0^{\otimes D}$, the [tensor product](tensor-product.md) of $D$ copies of $H_0$, one for each selected bit.

A simultaneous butterfly layer applies the two-point map of a [butterfly](butterfly.md) to one selected bit of each of several transform axes at once, computing the exact result in one tape procedure.
The layer acts on $D$ [transform axes](transform-axis.md), where $D$ is the number of axes.
The procedure ends with one final [truncation](truncation.md) of its values.

The layer groups the selected bits by [binary changes of basis](binary-change-of-basis.md), invertible row additions over the [binary field](binary-field.md) that relabel the bits, so that each group gives a smaller tensor product.
The layer is built from the [two-point kernel](two-point-kernel.md) $C$ on each selected bit.

symbols.name: number of axes
symbols.meaning: The number of transform axes that the layer acts on, one selected bit on each.
symbols.quote: The layer acts on $D$ [transform axes](transform-axis.md), where $D$ is the number of axes.

symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The number of consecutive address bits in each transform axis (chunk).
symbols.quote: Each axis is a chunk of $\delta$ consecutive address bits, where $\delta$ is the number of bits in each chunk.

symbols.name: selected offset
symbols.meaning: The position of the selected bit within its chunk, counted from the least significant end.
symbols.quote: In each chunk one bit is selected, at the same offset $o$ with $0\le o<\delta$, where $o$ is the position of the selected bit within its chunk, counted from the least significant end.

symbols.name: two-point map
symbols.meaning: The two-point map $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$, as a $2\times2$ matrix.
symbols.quote: Write $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$ for the two-point map, whose matrix is $H_0=\frac12\left(\begin{array}{cc}1&1\\1&-1\end{array}\right)$.

symbols.name: length-q transform
symbols.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform on $q$ values, normalized by $1/q$.
symbols.quote: Let $F_q$ be the transform with $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2π i jk/q}$, where $q$ is the number of values transformed, $j$ indexes the input values and $k$ the output coordinates.

symbols.name: number of values
symbols.meaning: The number of values that the transform $F_q$ acts on.
symbols.quote: Let $F_q$ be the transform with $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2π i jk/q}$, where $q$ is the number of values transformed, $j$ indexes the input values and $k$ the output coordinates.

symbols.name: input index
symbols.meaning: The index of an input value in the transform $F_q$.
symbols.quote: Let $F_q$ be the transform with $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2π i jk/q}$, where $q$ is the number of values transformed, $j$ indexes the input values and $k$ the output coordinates.

symbols.name: output index
symbols.meaning: The index of an output coordinate of the transform $F_q$.
symbols.quote: Let $F_q$ be the transform with $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2π i jk/q}$, where $q$ is the number of values transformed, $j$ indexes the input values and $k$ the output coordinates.

symbols.name: normalized Hadamard matrix
symbols.meaning: The $2\times2$ Hadamard matrix with the $1/\sqrt2$ normalization.
symbols.quote: The unitary normalization $1/\sqrt q$ gives the normalized Hadamard matrix $\mathcal H=\frac1{\sqrt2}\left(\begin{array}{cc}1&1\\1&-1\end{array}\right)=\sqrt2\,H_0$.

symbols.name: diagonal phase matrix
symbols.quote: Let $\Delta=\mathrm{diag}(1,i)$ be a diagonal phase matrix, $X=\left(\begin{array}{cc}0&1\\1&0\end{array}\right)$ the bit-flip matrix, and $I$ the $2\times2$ identity matrix.

symbols.name: bit-flip matrix
symbols.meaning: The $2\times2$ matrix that swaps the two basis states of one bit.
symbols.quote: Let $\Delta=\mathrm{diag}(1,i)$ be a diagonal phase matrix, $X=\left(\begin{array}{cc}0&1\\1&0\end{array}\right)$ the bit-flip matrix, and $I$ the $2\times2$ identity matrix.

symbols.name: identity matrix
symbols.quote: Let $\Delta=\mathrm{diag}(1,i)$ be a diagonal phase matrix, $X=\left(\begin{array}{cc}0&1\\1&0\end{array}\right)$ the bit-flip matrix, and $I$ the $2\times2$ identity matrix.

symbols.name: identity coefficient
symbols.meaning: The coefficient of $I$ in $C$, equal to $(1+i)/2$.
symbols.quote: Let $\lambda=(1+i)/2$ and $\mu=(1-i)/2$, where $\lambda$ is the coefficient of the identity $I$ and $\mu$ the coefficient of $X$.

symbols.name: bit-flip coefficient
symbols.meaning: The coefficient of $X$ in $C$, equal to $(1-i)/2$.
symbols.quote: Let $\lambda=(1+i)/2$ and $\mu=(1-i)/2$, where $\lambda$ is the coefficient of the identity $I$ and $\mu$ the coefficient of $X$.

symbols.name: two-point kernel
symbols.meaning: The two-by-two operator $\mathcal H\Delta\mathcal H$, equal to $\lambda I+\mu X$.
symbols.quote: Define $C=\mathcal H\Delta\mathcal H$, which equals $\lambda I+\mu X$.

symbols.name: address phase operator
symbols.meaning: The diagonal operator $\Delta^{\otimes D}$ that multiplies each address by $i$ to the number of selected bits equal to 1 there.
symbols.quote: Here $\Delta_D=\Delta^{\otimes D}$ multiplies the value at each address by $i$ raised to the number of selected bits equal to 1 there, so $\Delta_D$ is diagonal.

symbols.name: working precision
symbols.meaning: The working precision in bits: the inputs lie on the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$.
symbols.quote: Here $p$ is the working precision in bits.

symbols.name: number of H_0 factors
symbols.meaning: The number of individual factors $H_0$ applied, which refines the grid to $2^{-(p+s)}$.
symbols.quote: Here $s$ changes meaning and counts the individual factors $H_0$ applied.
